title: Bump Python 3.8 base image (server/Dockerfile) alongside ML stack rework
description: server/Dockerfile is on python:3.8-slim (EOL Oct 2024). UPDATE from jtc.1: the ML replacement did NOT end up needing this - torch==2.4.1, tokenizers==0.20.3, transformers==4.46.3 all still ship cp38 wheels, so bert-extractive-summarizer was replaced without touching Python. The real coupling is with jtc.3 (Django bump): Django 3.1.4 only supports Python up to 3.8, and the remaining ancient cp38-pinned scientific stack (numpy==1.19.4, scipy==1.6.0, pandas==1.2.0, matplotlib==3.3.3, scikit-learn==0.24.0) would all need bumping together with any Python bump, since none of those have wheels for a modern Python either. This is now effectively the same undertaking as jtc.3, not a prerequisite for it - do them together.
acceptance_criteria: server/Dockerfile builds on a current, non-EOL Python version; full requirements.txt resolves and installs cleanly; all 24 smoke tests pass.

title: Django 3.1.4 -> 5.2 LTS major version bump
description: server/core/settings.py's Django is 5+ major versions behind current LTS (5.2). Needs per-dependency compat checks for django-organizations==2.0.0, dj-rest-auth==2.1.2, django_celery_beat==2.1.0, django-filter==2.4.0, django_extensions==3.1.0, djangorestframework==3.12.2 - each has its own Django-version support matrix. Known breaking changes to handle: USE_L10N removed in Django 5.0 (currently set True in settings.py line ~138), DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD warnings since 3.2, possible url()->re_path() usage. Recommend stepping through intermediate LTS versions (3.2 -> 4.2 -> 5.2) rather than jumping directly, running the smoke test suite at each step.
acceptance_criteria: python manage.py check and python manage.py migrate run clean on Django 5.2; all 24 existing smoke tests pass; each third-party app (organizations, dj_rest_auth, django_celery_beat, django_filters, django_extensions) confirmed compatible with 5.2.
notes: UPDATE from jtc.1/jtc.2 work: Django 3.1.4 only supports Python up to 3.8, so this bump is now coupled with jtc.2 (Python base image bump) - do them together, along with the remaining cp38-pinned scientific stack (numpy==1.19.4, scipy==1.6.0, pandas==1.2.0, matplotlib==3.3.3, scikit-learn==0.24.0), none of which have wheels for a modern Python either. This is the single largest remaining piece of Phase 2 - budget real per-step verification time (smoke tests + manage.py check + manage.py migrate at each intermediate LTS step).

title: Replace bert-extractive-summarizer with direct transformers pipeline call
description: server/bert/src/bertSummarizer.py currently does: from summarizer import Summarizer; model = Summarizer(); model(text, min_length=60). That's the entire integration surface (wired via server/bert/tasks.py's bert_job Celery task). bert-extractive-summarizer==0.6.1 tightly pins torch==1.7.1 and transformers==4.1.1 (2020-era). Replace with a direct call into a current transformers summarization pipeline, keeping the same call site/task interface.
acceptance_criteria: server/bert app's smoke tests (server/bert/tests.py) still pass; bert_job Celery task still produces a text summary from a Bert model row; torch/transformers versions in requirements.txt are current, not the 2020-era pins.
close_reason: Replaced bert-extractive-summarizer with a direct transformers pipeline call (facebook/bart-large-cnn), verified end-to-end (real summary produced) and via the 24-test smoke suite.

title: Phase 2: Server modernization (Django LTS + ML stack replacement)
description: Follow-up to Phase 0/1 (docker-compose WSL fix + security hardening, commit a39f881). Zero test coverage existed before Phase 1 added minimal DRF smoke tests per app (24 tests) - use those as the regression signal for this phase. See ~/.claude/plans/async-cooking-globe.md for full Phase 1 writeup and rationale.
design: User explicitly chose: replace bert-extractive-summarizer rather than upgrade-in-place or leave pinned. Django jump should go through django-organizations/dj-rest-auth/django_celery_beat/django-filter/django_extensions compat checks per version, not straight 3.1->5.2. Bundle the Python 3.8 base image bump with the ML rework since the pinned ML wheels are tied to that CPython ABI.

title: Bump react-admin 3.14.1 -> 4/5 and @material-ui v4 -> @mui v5
description: Breaking changes across ra-core/ra-ui-materialui APIs and MUI's v4->v5 rename (@material-ui/core -> @mui/material, styled-components/makeStyles changes, @material-ui/data-grid v4-alpha -> @mui/x-data-grid). Touches all ~13 feature folders' List/Show/Edit/Create components since they're built directly on react-admin's <Resource> model. ra-data-django-rest-framework==0.1.5 data provider also pinned to the v3 API shape - verify its compatibility or replace.
acceptance_criteria: yarn build succeeds without the react-scripts 4 openssl-legacy-provider workaround being load-bearing for a *new* incompatibility; new smoke tests (see sibling task) pass; every resource's List/Show/Edit/Create still renders.

title: Write minimal admin frontend smoke tests before react-admin migration
description: admin/src/App.test.js is unmodified CRA boilerplate (asserts 'renders learn react link', which will fail since the app doesn't render that). Zero real coverage exists. Add a minimal render-smoke test per resource (or at least per feature folder) using @testing-library/react before attempting the react-admin/MUI major bump, mirroring the rationale for Phase 1's server-side DRF smoke tests.

title: Phase 3: Admin frontend modernization (react-admin v3->v5, MUI v4->v5)
description: admin/ is a small, boilerplate-heavy react-admin dashboard (62 files across ~13 feature folders: bert, extractor, dashboard, lighthouse, lighthouseResults, security, securityResults, sitemap, website, yake, layout, custom - each a thin List/Show/Edit/Create pair). Currently react-admin==3.14.1, @material-ui/core v4 (via react-admin's own deps), react==17. Phase 1 unblocked the build itself (postcss/openssl fixes, commit a39f881) but did not touch these app-level majors. CRA was never ejected, no custom webpack config - favors an in-place dependency bump over a Vite migration. Zero real test coverage exists (App.test.js is unmodified CRA boilerplate that doesn't match the app) - write at least minimal smoke coverage before attempting this, same rationale as Phase 1's server-side smoke tests.
design: Do this only after frontend has some smoke-test safety net, per user's phased/safety-first preference from the Phase 1 planning conversation.

title: Verify/refresh yake pinned-commit dependency
description: requirements.txt pins yake from a git commit (git+https://github.com/LIAAD/yake@481b684...) rather than PyPI, predating the package's PyPI releases (now yake==0.4.3 resolves from PyPI per Phase 1's pip resolution log). server/keywords/tasks.py's usage is narrow: yake.KeywordExtractor(lan=language, ...).extract_keywords(text). Confirm switching to the PyPI release keeps this API working, then drop the git+ pin.
acceptance_criteria: server/keywords smoke tests pass; requirements.txt no longer needs a git+ URL for yake.
close_reason: Switched yake from a pinned git commit to yake==0.4.8 from PyPI (latest 0.7.3 requires Python >=3.10, deferred to the Python bump). Verified KeywordExtractor/extract_keywords API unchanged.
